title: Hackers hid dangerous malware on a page hidden in Anthopic's Claude.ai domain
excerpt: Claude Artifacts have been used as phishing lures, once again
content_html:
• Huntress spots malicious Claude Artifact spoofing Claude Desktop, spreading SectopRAT malware
  • Victims were redirected via Bing ads, infecting at least 29 organizations between July 21–22, 2026
  • Claude removed the artifact after 7,000+ views; malvertising risks persist despite disclaimers on artifacts

At least 29 organizations have been infected with a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) after mistaking a public Claude Artifact for a legitimate Claude page.

A Claude Artifact is an interactive document, or piece of code, that the AI generates and then hosts on the Claude platform. It can then be shared with other people as an example, or proof of concept, for different solutions. The link to an artifact usually looks something like this:

claude[.]ai/public/artifacts/ca466f1f-21c0-42af-b329-8f1c7534a891

Claude Artifacts are often used for phishing and other forms of scams, and we’ve seen it in ClickFix attacks in the past. Claude responded by adding a disclaimer to every artifact, stating that the content is user-generated and thus unverified.

In this particular case, a malicious artifact was created to spoof the download page for Claude Desktop. Victims would get redirected to an attacker-controlled domain, where instead of the Claude app, they’d download SectopRAT, a remote access trojan capable of stealing credit card data, personal information, files, passwords, and more.

The artifact was then promoted on Bing, showing up at the very top of search results to people searching for “Claude Desktop App”.

For years, the cybersecurity community has warned about malvertising, urging users to double-check the domain before clicking on any links, even promoted ones. However, the problem here is that the ad takes the victims to the legitimate Claude domain, making scrutiny that much harder.

The campaign was spotted by security researchers Huntress, who said that between July 21 and July 22, 2026, their SOC “lit up with a swathe of unusual executable installs, Defender exclusions, and anomalous persistence across 29 organizations, all coming from ClaudeDesktop.exe.”

Claude has since removed the malicious artifact, but not before it raked up more than 7,000 views. It is possible that other organizations, outside Huntress’ field of view, also fell victim to this scam.

content_html_zh:
• Huntress 发现恶意 Claude Artifact 欺骗 Claude Desktop，传播 SectopRAT 恶意软件
  • 受害者通过 Bing 广告进行重定向，在 2026 年 7 月 21 日至 22 日期间感染了至少 29 个组织
  • 克劳德在观看次数超过 7,000 次后删除了该工件；尽管对文物有免责声明，但恶意广告风险仍然存在

至少有 29 个组织将公共 Claude Artifact 误认为合法的 Claude 页面，从而感染了远程访问特洛伊木马 (RAT)。

Claude Artifact 是人工智能生成并托管在 Claude 平台上的交互式文档或代码。 然后可以将其作为不同解决方案的示例或概念证明与其他人共享。 工件的链接通常如下所示：

克劳德[.]ai/public/artifacts/ca466f1f-21c0-42af-b329-8f1c7534a891

Claude Artifacts 通常用于网络钓鱼和其他形式的诈骗，我们过去在 ClickFix 攻击中也看到过这种情况。 克劳德对此做出回应，为每个工件添加了免责声明，声明内容是用户生成的，因此未经验证。

在这种特殊情况下，创建了一个恶意工件来欺骗 Claude Desktop 的下载页面。 受害者将被重定向到攻击者控制的域，在那里他们会下载 SectopRAT，而不是 Claude 应用程序，这是一种远程访问木马，能够窃取信用卡数据、个人信息、文件、密码等。

随后，该工件在 Bing 上进行了推广，在搜索“Claude Desktop App”的用户中显示在搜索结果的最顶部。

多年来，网络安全社区一直对恶意广告发出警告，敦促用户在点击任何链接（甚至是推广链接）之前仔细检查域名。 然而，这里的问题是，该广告将受害者带到了合法的克劳德域名，这使得审查变得更加困难。

安全研究人员 Huntress 发现了该活动，她表示，2026 年 7 月 21 日至 22 日期间，他们的 SOC“在 29 个组织中出现了一系列异常可执行安装、Defender 排除和异常持久性，所有这些都来自 ClaudeDesktop.exe。”

此后，Claude 删除了该恶意工件，但在此之前它已获得超过 7,000 次浏览。 女猎手视野之外的其他组织也可能成为这一骗局的受害者。
